newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent looks firmer but others stay weak.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent looks firmer but others stay weak.

text.p: Most North Sea spot crudes were under pressure on Wednesday from an overhang of prompt barrels but benchmark Dated Brent and later barrels were looking marginally firmer, traders said.
Dated Brent was offered at Sept Brent -20 cents for a Sept 5-7 cargo and at -15 cents for barrels loading four days later. The last reported Brent deal was at Sept -25 cents.
"It's looking a bit brighter further out but there's still a bit of work to be done at the front end," said a trader.
One of two Brents turning wet on Wednesday was kept by BP. Chevron was clocked with the other but was seeking a deferral.
Of the other North Sea grades, Norwegian Statfjord and Oseberg were still the most vulnerable with supply fairly lengthy, traders said.

A Sept 14-16 Statfjord traded at Dated Brent +15/+18 cents, four or five cents weaker than the last deal. An Oseberg cargo loading Sept 11-13 was heard done at Dated Brent +15 cents, with late pricing.

Ekofisk, however, was looking steadier and traded at Dated Brent +35 cents, underpinned by talk of persistent production problems which forced operator Phillips on Wednesday to defer Sept 10-17 loadings by a day.
Oct Brent gained about 38 cents to $20.41 by 1758 GMT, but intermonth spreads were unchanged from early levels. Oct/Nov traded at +38 and +40 cents while Nov/Dec fetched +38 cents.
Mediterranean trade saw much of the distressed Urals crude taken off the market. One of the 80,000-tonne cargoes sold at Dated Brent -$1.10 a barrel.

Another, larger cargo loading around the same time was heard sold and although details were unclear, some traders suggested it could sail transatlantic after a million barrels moved to the U.S late last week. A third end-August cargo (80,000 tonnes) was thought headed for the French-based lifter's system in Lavera.
"It (trade) helped a lot today," one trader said adding that later cargoes were expected to fetch between Dated -80/90 cents.
The terminal at Novorossiisk remained shut late Wednesday afternoon due to poor weather conditions.
"It's still shut and it looks set to continue," a shipping source said.
Little Iranian Heavy was seen offered for September. Sellers were asking Dated Brent -$1.60.

"The prices just have not followed Urals down but Iranian sellers are not under any pressure so they are just sitting back and waiting," one potential buyer said adding that Iranian Heavy was currently the favoured crude for his system.
